blocks.text:
# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).
#
# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. The baseline (per-function CRAP of everything above
# CRAP_THRESHOLD) is NOT in the repository — with many agents opening PRs a committed file
# conflicts constantly. It lives in a rolling GitHub release asset:
#
#   release tag  crap-baseline   (prerelease, never "latest" — agent pack consumers resolve
#                                 releases/latest, so this one must not be it)
#   asset        crap-baseline.json
#
# pull_request / workflow_dispatch (the factory SM dispatches this on PR heads): measure the
#   head and COMPARE with the released baseline. Fails when a function's CRAP grew or a new
#   function exceeds CRAP_THRESHOLD; labels crap:regression / crap:improved.
# main (push, merge-bot completion via workflow_run — the bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, which
#   never fires 'push' —, or manual dispatch on main): after a green measurement, ratchet the
#   released baseline DOWN (crap4js --update-baseline: min(old, now), never up, refuses on
#   regression) and upload it. The release notes carry 'main@<sha>' so repeated triggers for
#   the same HEAD are skipped. Concurrent merges are serialized by the concurrency group.
# No baseline asset yet (first run / fork): bootstrap from the measured main, no comparison.
#
# Coverage comes from the unit suite run in the same job (instrumented tree), so the
# ratchet is evaluated with the unit-test results of the head.
#
# Tool pin: IstiN/crap4js by commit SHA (fork of vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js v0.15.0 +
# --baseline / --update-baseline, pipe-safe exit). Installed from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js'
# package is an unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_run:
    # The merge bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, and GitHub suppresses workflow triggers on
    # GITHUB_TOKEN events — the push trigger above never fires for machine merges (same
    # reason agent-pack-release.yml listens to this workflow, gh-867). The bot's own run
    # completion is a normal event. Runs on every bot completion are cheap no-ops: the
    # 'gate' job skips when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
    workflows: ['Machine Merge Bot']
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs; on main it re-seeds the baseline

permissions:
  contents: write        # push to main: update the crap-baseline release asset
  pull-requests: write   # crap:regression / crap:improved labels

# Serializes baseline updates of consecutive merges (never cancels a running update).
concurrency:
  group: quality-${{ (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_run' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/main') && 'baseline-update' || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  # Threshold for functions NOT in crap-baseline.json (new or renamed code).
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '8'
  CRAP4JS_REPO: 'IstiN/crap4js'
  CRAP4JS_REF: '83ee6201e554a91d51c298f045c5c4cb47317b6d'
  BASELINE_TAG: 'crap-baseline'
  BASELINE_ASSET: 'crap-baseline.json'

jobs:
  gate:
    # PR / dispatch on a PR head: always measure. Main-side events (push, merge-bot completion,
    # manual dispatch on main): measure only when the released baseline does not yet cover HEAD.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.g.outputs.run }}
    steps:
      - id: g
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          REF: ${{ github.ref }}
          BOT_CONCLUSION: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.conclusion }}
        run: |
          main_side=false
          [ "$EVENT" = "push" ] || [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && main_side=true
          [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_dispatch" ] && [ "$REF" = "refs/heads/main" ] && main_side=true
          if [ "$main_side" != "true" ]; then
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0      # pull_request / dispatch on a PR head: always measure
          fi
          if [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && [ "$BOT_CONCLUSION" != "success" ]; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "merge bot run was not successful — skip"; exit 0
          fi
          body="$(gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json body --jq .body 2>/dev/null || true)"
          if printf '%s' "$body" | grep -q "main@${GITHUB_SHA}"; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "baseline already covers ${GITHUB_SHA} — skip"
          else
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

content.text:
node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          exit $code

      - name: Update the released baseline (main only — ratchets down, never up)
        if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.event_name != 'pull_request' && (steps.ratchet.outcome == 'success' || steps.baseline.outputs.present != 'true')
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -e
          CRAP="$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js"
          NOTES="Rolling per-function CRAP baseline used by the Quality workflow. Updated after every merge to main; not a product release. Measured at main@${GITHUB_SHA}"
          OUT="$RUNNER_TEMP/baseline-out/$BASELINE_ASSET"
          mkdir -p "$(dirname "$OUT")"
          # Full report (every function) for the README badges; ratchet steps keep their own outputs.
          "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold 99999 > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap-all.txt" || true
          if [ "${{ steps.baseline.outputs.present }}" = "true" ]; then
            cp "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" "$OUT"
            "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold "$CRAP_THRESHOLD" \
              --baseline "$OUT" --update-baseline > "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt"
            sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
            if cmp -s "$OUT" "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET"; then
              echo "baseline unchanged — nothing to upload (marker refreshed)"
              gh release edit "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --notes "$NOTES"
              exit 0
            fi
          else
            "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold "$CRAP_THRESHOLD" \
              --baseline "$OUT" --write-baseline > "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt"
          fi
          tail -1 "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt"
          if gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            gh release upload "$BASELINE_TAG" "$OUT" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --clobber
          else
            gh release create "$BASELINE_TAG" "$OUT" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --prerelease --latest=false \
              --title "CRAP baseline (rolling)" \
              --notes "Rolling per-function CRAP baseline used by the Quality workflow. Updated after every merge to main; not a product release."
          fi
          # Marker the 'gate' job reads to skip runs when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
          gh release edit "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --notes "$NOTES"
          echo "baseline released: $(node -e "const b=require('$OUT');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

      - name: Publish README badges (main only — data lives on the 'badges' branch)

re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. blocks.text:
# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).
#
# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. The baseline (per-function CRAP of everything above
# CRAP_THRESHOLD) is NOT in the repository — with many agents opening PRs a committed file
# conflicts constantly. It lives in a rolling GitHub release asset:
#
#   release tag  crap-baseline   (prerelease, never "latest" — agent pack consumers resolve
#                                 releases/latest, so this one must not be it)
#   asset        crap-baseline.json
#
# pull_request / workflow_dispatch (the factory SM dispatches this on PR heads): measure the
#   head and COMPARE with the released baseline. Fails when a function's CRAP grew or a new
#   function exceeds CRAP_THRESHOLD; labels crap:regression / crap:improved.
# main (push, merge-bot completion via workflow_run — the bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, which
#   never fires 'push' —, or manual dispatch on main): after a green measurement, ratchet the
#   released baseline DOWN (crap4js --update-baseline: min(old, now), never up, refuses on
#   regression) and upload it. The release notes carry 'main@<sha>' so repeated triggers for
#   the same HEAD are skipped. Concurrent merges are serialized by the concurrency group.
# No baseline asset yet (first run / fork): bootstrap from the measured main, no comparison.
#
# Coverage comes from the unit suite run in the same job (instrumented tree), so the
# ratchet is evaluated with the unit-test results of the head.
#
# Tool pin: IstiN/crap4js by commit SHA (fork of vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js v0.15.0 +
# --baseline / --update-baseline, pipe-safe exit). Installed from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js'
# package is an unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_run:
    # The merge bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, and GitHub suppresses workflow triggers on
    # GITHUB_TOKEN events — the push trigger above never fires for machine merges (same
    # reason agent-pack-release.yml listens to this workflow, gh-867). The bot's own run
    # completion is a normal event. Runs on every bot completion are cheap no-ops: the
    # 'gate' job skips when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
    workflows: ['Machine Merge Bot']
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs; on main it re-seeds the baseline

permissions:
  contents: write        # push to main: update the crap-baseline release asset
  pull-requests: write   # crap:regression / crap:improved labels

# Serializes baseline updates of consecutive merges (never cancels a running update).
concurrency:
  group: quality-${{ (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_run' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/main') && 'baseline-update' || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  # Threshold for functions NOT in crap-baseline.json (new or renamed code).
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '8'
  CRAP4JS_REPO: 'IstiN/crap4js'
  CRAP4JS_REF: '83ee6201e554a91d51c298f045c5c4cb47317b6d'
  BASELINE_TAG: 'crap-baseline'
  BASELINE_ASSET: 'crap-baseline.json'

jobs:
  gate:
    # PR / dispatch on a PR head: always measure. Main-side events (push, merge-bot completion,
    # manual dispatch on main): measure only when the released baseline does not yet cover HEAD.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.g.outputs.run }}
    steps:
      - id: g
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          REF: ${{ github.ref }}
          BOT_CONCLUSION: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.conclusion }}
        run: |
          main_side=false
          [ "$EVENT" = "push" ] || [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && main_side=true
          [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_dispatch" ] && [ "$REF" = "refs/heads/main" ] && main_side=true
          if [ "$main_side" != "true" ]; then
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0      # pull_request / dispatch on a PR head: always measure

node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          exit $code

      - name: Update the released baseline (main only — ratchets down, never up)
        if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.event_name != 'pull_request' && (steps.ratchet.outcome == 'success' || steps.baseline.outputs.present != 'true')
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -e
          CRAP="$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js"
          NOTES="Rolling per-function CRAP baseline used by the Quality workflow. Updated after every merge to main; not a product release. Measured at main@${GITHUB_SHA}"
          OUT="$RUNNER_TEMP/baseline-out/$BASELINE_ASSET"
          mkdir -p "$(dirname "$OUT")"
          # Full report (every function) for the README badges; ratchet steps keep their own outputs.
          "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold 99999 > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap-all.txt" || true
          if [ "${{ steps.baseline.outputs.present }}" = "true" ]; then
            cp "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" "$OUT"
            "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold "$CRAP_THRESHOLD" \
              --baseline "$OUT" --update-baseline > "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt"
            sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
            if cmp -s "$OUT" "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET"; then
              echo "baseline unchanged — nothing to upload (marker refreshed)"
              gh release edit "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --notes "$NOTES"
              exit 0
            fi
          else
            "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold "$CRAP_THRESHOLD" \
              --baseline "$OUT" --write-baseline > "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt"
          fi
          tail -1 "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt"
          if gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            gh release upload "$BASELINE_TAG" "$OUT" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --clobber
          else
            gh release create "$BASELINE_TAG" "$OUT" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --prerelease --latest=false \
              --title "CRAP baseline (rolling)" \
              --notes "Rolling per-function CRAP baseline used by the Quality workflow. Updated after every merge to main; not a product release."
          fi
          # Marker the 'gate' job reads to skip runs when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
          gh release edit "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --notes "$NOTES"
          echo "baseline released: $(node -e "const b=require('$OUT');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

      - name: Publish README badges (main only — data lives on the 'badges' branch)

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. callers/callees of changed symbols,

impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality

BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. # gh-1037: [CRAP] writeContentOutput.action (62) + writeSolutionAndLabels.buildMarkdownSection (42)

## Description

## Problem
`js/writeContentOutput.js::action` **61.9** and `js/writeSolutionAndLabels.js::buildMarkdownSection` **42** write generated content and labels back to trackers. Output text and tracker payloads must stay byte-identical.

## Goal
Bring each named function under CRAP 30 by extracting pure parse/build/decide helpers and covering every branch with characterization tests. Same tracker/SCM/git/file calls in the same order.

## Acceptance
- Behaviour unchanged; each named function at or below the target; no regression; CI `crap` check green and the node harness stays green (canonical runner: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`).
- No code path removed; uncovered paths get a characterization test.

## Rules (read before starting)
- **Pure refactor, behaviour-preserving, backward compatible.** Same exports, same signatures, same return shapes, same log lines/side effects, same tracker/SCM calls in the same order. No config or API changes.
- **Tests first:** add characterization tests that pin the current behaviour of the paths you touch (the node harness: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`), then extract pure helpers (`parse*`/`build*`/`decide*`) from the big function and test those directly. Raising coverage on the function counts as much as splitting it.
- **CRAP gate:** Quality/`crap` compares this PR with the released baseline (`crap-baseline` release). The target function must go DOWN, no function may go up, new functions must be <= 8 (CRAP = CC² + CC at 0% coverage, so an untested helper needs CC <= 2 — or cover it). `crap:improved` is set automatically when it dropped. The baseline is updated by CI after the merge — do **not** commit a baseline file.
- Measure locally: `node ci/run_with_coverage.js …` then `crap4js . --coverage … --threshold 8 --baseline <released crap-baseline.json>` (see .github/workflows/quality.yml).
- Do not "fix" CRAP by deleting tests, adding `/* istanbul ignore */`, or excluding files.

blocks.text:
# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).
#
# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. The baseline (per-function CRAP of everything above
# CRAP_THRESHOLD) is NOT in the repository — with many agents opening PRs a committed file
# conflicts constantly. It lives in a rolling GitHub release asset:
#
#   release tag  crap-baseline   (prerelease, never "latest" — agent pack consumers resolve
#                                 releases/latest, so this one must not be it)
#   asset        crap-baseline.json
#
# pull_request / workflow_dispatch (the factory SM dispatches this on PR heads): measure the
#   head and COMPARE with the released baseline. Fails when a function's CRAP grew or a new
#   function exceeds CRAP_THRESHOLD; labels crap:regression / crap:improved.
# main (push, merge-bot completion via workflow_run — the bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, which
#   never fires 'push' —, or manual dispatch on main): after a green measurement, ratchet the
#   released baseline DOWN (crap4js --update-baseline: min(old, now), never up, refuses on
#   regression) and upload it. The release notes carry 'main@<sha>' so repeated triggers for
#   the same HEAD are skipped. Concurrent merges are serialized by the concurrency group.
# No baseline asset yet (first run / fork): bootstrap from the measured main, no comparison.
#
# Coverage comes from the unit suite run in the same job (instrumented tree), so the
# ratchet is evaluated with the unit-test results of the head.
#
# Tool pin: IstiN/crap4js by commit SHA (fork of vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js v0.15.0 +
# --baseline / --update-baseline, pipe-safe exit). Installed from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js'
# package is an unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_run:
    # The merge bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, and GitHub suppresses workflow triggers on
    # GITHUB_TOKEN events — the push trigger above never fires for machine merges (same
    # reason agent-pack-release.yml listens to this workflow, gh-867). The bot's own run
    # completion is a normal event. Runs on every bot completion are cheap no-ops: the
    # 'gate' job skips when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
    workflows: ['Machine Merge Bot']
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs; on main it re-seeds the baseline

permissions:
  contents: write        # push to main: update the crap-baseline release asset
  pull-requests: write   # crap:regression / crap:improved labels

# Serializes baseline updates of consecutive merges (never cancels a running update).
concurrency:
  group: quality-${{ (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_run' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/main') && 'baseline-update' || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  # Threshold for functions NOT in crap-baseline.json (new or renamed code).
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '8'
  CRAP4JS_REPO: 'IstiN/crap4js'
  CRAP4JS_REF: '83ee6201e554a91d51c298f045c5c4cb47317b6d'
  BASELINE_TAG: 'crap-baseline'
  BASELINE_ASSET: 'crap-baseline.json'

jobs:
  gate:
    # PR / dispatch on a PR head: always measure. Main-side events (push, merge-bot completion,
    # manual dispatch on main): measure only when the released baseline does not yet cover HEAD.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.g.outputs.run }}
    steps:
      - id: g
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          REF: ${{ github.ref }}
          BOT_CONCLUSION: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.conclusion }}
        run: |
          main_side=false
          [ "$EVENT" = "push" ] || [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && main_side=true
          [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_dispatch" ] && [ "$REF" = "refs/heads/main" ] && main_side=true
          if [ "$main_side" != "true" ]; then
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0      # pull_request / dispatch on a PR head: always measure
          fi
          if [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && [ "$BOT_CONCLUSION" != "success" ]; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "merge bot run was not successful — skip"; exit 0
          fi
          body="$(gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json body --jq .body 2>/dev/null || true)"
          if printf '%s' "$body" | grep -q "main@${GITHUB_SHA}"; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "baseline already covers ${GITHUB_SHA} — skip"
          else
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          exit $code

      - name: Update the released baseline (main only — ratchets down, never up)
        if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.event_name != 'pull_request' && (steps.ratchet.outcome == 'success' || steps.baseline.outputs.present != 'true')
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -e
          CRAP="$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js"
          NOTES="Rolling per-function CRAP baseline used by the Quality workflow. Updated after every merge to main; not a product release. Measured at main@${GITHUB_SHA}"
          OUT="$RUNNER_TEMP/baseline-out/$BASELINE_ASSET"
          mkdir -p "$(dirname "$OUT")"
          # Full report (every function) for the README badges; ratchet steps keep their own outputs.
          "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold 99999 > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap-all.txt" || true
          if [ "${{ steps.baseline.outputs.present }}" = "true" ]; then
            cp "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" "$OUT"
            "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold "$CRAP_THRESHOLD" \
              --baseline "$OUT" --update-baseline > "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt"
            sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
            if cmp -s "$OUT" "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET"; then
              echo "baseline unchanged — nothing to upload (marker refreshed)"
              gh release edit "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --notes "$NOTES"
              exit 0
            fi
          else
            "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold "$CRAP_THRESHOLD" \
              --baseline "$OUT" --write-baseline > "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt"
          fi
          tail -1 "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt"
          if gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            gh release upload "$BASELINE_TAG" "$OUT" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --clobber
          else
            gh release create "$BASELINE_TAG" "$OUT" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --prerelease --latest=false \
              --title "CRAP baseline (rolling)" \
              --notes "Rolling per-function CRAP baseline used by the Quality workflow. Updated after every merge to main; not a product release."
          fi
          # Marker the 'gate' job reads to skip runs when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
          gh release edit "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --notes "$NOTES"
          echo "baseline released: $(node -e "const b=require('$OUT');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

      - name: Publish README badges (main only — data lives on the 'badges' branch)

blocks.text:
# Quality gate — per-function CRAP ratchet via crap4js (IstiN fork).
#
# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. The baseline (per-function CRAP of everything above
# CRAP_THRESHOLD) is NOT in the repository — with many agents opening PRs a committed file
# conflicts constantly. It lives in a rolling GitHub release asset:
#
#   release tag  crap-baseline   (prerelease, never "latest" — agent pack consumers resolve
#                                 releases/latest, so this one must not be it)
#   asset        crap-baseline.json
#
# pull_request / workflow_dispatch (the factory SM dispatches this on PR heads): measure the
#   head and COMPARE with the released baseline. Fails when a function's CRAP grew or a new
#   function exceeds CRAP_THRESHOLD; labels crap:regression / crap:improved.
# main (push, merge-bot completion via workflow_run — the bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, which
#   never fires 'push' —, or manual dispatch on main): after a green measurement, ratchet the
#   released baseline DOWN (crap4js --update-baseline: min(old, now), never up, refuses on
#   regression) and upload it. The release notes carry 'main@<sha>' so repeated triggers for
#   the same HEAD are skipped. Concurrent merges are serialized by the concurrency group.
# No baseline asset yet (first run / fork): bootstrap from the measured main, no comparison.
#
# Coverage comes from the unit suite run in the same job (instrumented tree), so the
# ratchet is evaluated with the unit-test results of the head.
#
# Tool pin: IstiN/crap4js by commit SHA (fork of vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js v0.15.0 +
# --baseline / --update-baseline, pipe-safe exit). Installed from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js'
# package is an unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_run:
    # The merge bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, and GitHub suppresses workflow triggers on
    # GITHUB_TOKEN events — the push trigger above never fires for machine merges (same
    # reason agent-pack-release.yml listens to this workflow, gh-867). The bot's own run
    # completion is a normal event. Runs on every bot completion are cheap no-ops: the
    # 'gate' job skips when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
    workflows: ['Machine Merge Bot']
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs; on main it re-seeds the baseline

permissions:
  contents: write        # push to main: update the crap-baseline release asset
  pull-requests: write   # crap:regression / crap:improved labels

# Serializes baseline updates of consecutive merges (never cancels a running update).
concurrency:
  group: quality-${{ (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_run' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/main') && 'baseline-update' || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  # Threshold for functions NOT in crap-baseline.json (new or renamed code).
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '8'
  CRAP4JS_REPO: 'IstiN/crap4js'
  CRAP4JS_REF: '83ee6201e554a91d51c298f045c5c4cb47317b6d'
  BASELINE_TAG: 'crap-baseline'
  BASELINE_ASSET: 'crap-baseline.json'

jobs:
  gate:
    # PR / dispatch on a PR head: always measure. Main-side events (push, merge-bot completion,
    # manual dispatch on main): measure only when the released baseline does not yet cover HEAD.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.g.outputs.run }}
    steps:
      - id: g
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          REF: ${{ github.ref }}
          BOT_CONCLUSION: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.conclusion }}
        run: |
          main_side=false
          [ "$EVENT" = "push" ] || [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && main_side=true
          [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_dispatch" ] && [ "$REF" = "refs/heads/main" ] && main_side=true
          if [ "$main_side" != "true" ]; then
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0      # pull_request / dispatch on a PR head: always measure
          fi
          if [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && [ "$BOT_CONCLUSION" != "success" ]; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "merge bot run was not successful — skip"; exit 0
          fi
          body="$(gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json body --jq .body 2>/dev/null || true)"
          if printf '%s' "$body" | grep -q "main@${GITHUB_SHA}"; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "baseline already covers ${GITHUB_SHA} — skip"
          else
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          exit $code

      - name: Update the released baseline (main only — ratchets down, never up)
        if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.event_name != 'pull_request' && (steps.ratchet.outcome == 'success' || steps.baseline.outputs.present != 'true')
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -e
          CRAP="$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js"
          NOTES="Rolling per-function CRAP baseline used by the Quality workflow. Updated after every merge to main; not a product release. Measured at main@${GITHUB_SHA}"
          OUT="$RUNNER_TEMP/baseline-out/$BASELINE_ASSET"
          mkdir -p "$(dirname "$OUT")"
          # Full report (every function) for the README badges; ratchet steps keep their own outputs.
          "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold 99999 > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap-all.txt" || true
          if [ "${{ steps.baseline.outputs.present }}" = "true" ]; then
            cp "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" "$OUT"
            "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold "$CRAP_THRESHOLD" \
              --baseline "$OUT" --update-baseline > "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt"
            sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
            if cmp -s "$OUT" "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET"; then
              echo "baseline unchanged — nothing to upload (marker refreshed)"
              gh release edit "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --notes "$NOTES"
              exit 0
            fi
          else
            "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold "$CRAP_THRESHOLD" \
              --baseline "$OUT" --write-baseline > "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt"
          fi
          tail -1 "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt"
          if gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            gh release upload "$BASELINE_TAG" "$OUT" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --clobber
          else
            gh release create "$BASELINE_TAG" "$OUT" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --prerelease --latest=false \
              --title "CRAP baseline (rolling)" \
              --notes "Rolling per-function CRAP baseline used by the Quality workflow. Updated after every merge to main; not a product release."
          fi
          # Marker the 'gate' job reads to skip runs when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
          gh release edit "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --notes "$NOTES"
          echo "baseline released: $(node -e "const b=require('$OUT');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

      - name: Publish README badges (main only — data lives on the 'badges' branch)

# Policy: CRAP may only DECREASE. The baseline (per-function CRAP of everything above
# CRAP_THRESHOLD) is NOT in the repository — with many agents opening PRs a committed file
# conflicts constantly. It lives in a rolling GitHub release asset:
#
#   release tag  crap-baseline   (prerelease, never "latest" — agent pack consumers resolve
#                                 releases/latest, so this one must not be it)
#   asset        crap-baseline.json
#
# pull_request / workflow_dispatch (the factory SM dispatches this on PR heads): measure the
#   head and COMPARE with the released baseline. Fails when a function's CRAP grew or a new
#   function exceeds CRAP_THRESHOLD; labels crap:regression / crap:improved.
# main (push, merge-bot completion via workflow_run — the bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, which
#   never fires 'push' —, or manual dispatch on main): after a green measurement, ratchet the
#   released baseline DOWN (crap4js --update-baseline: min(old, now), never up, refuses on
#   regression) and upload it. The release notes carry 'main@<sha>' so repeated triggers for
#   the same HEAD are skipped. Concurrent merges are serialized by the concurrency group.
# No baseline asset yet (first run / fork): bootstrap from the measured main, no comparison.
#
# Coverage comes from the unit suite run in the same job (instrumented tree), so the
# ratchet is evaluated with the unit-test results of the head.
#
# Tool pin: IstiN/crap4js by commit SHA (fork of vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit/crap4js v0.15.0 +
# --baseline / --update-baseline, pipe-safe exit). Installed from GitHub — the npm 'crap4js'
# package is an unrelated third-party project.
name: Quality

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_run:
    # The merge bot merges with GITHUB_TOKEN, and GitHub suppresses workflow triggers on
    # GITHUB_TOKEN events — the push trigger above never fires for machine merges (same
    # reason agent-pack-release.yml listens to this workflow, gh-867). The bot's own run
    # completion is a normal event. Runs on every bot completion are cheap no-ops: the
    # 'gate' job skips when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
    workflows: ['Machine Merge Bot']
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:  # the Machine SM / sm-kicker dispatch validation runs; on main it re-seeds the baseline

permissions:
  contents: write        # push to main: update the crap-baseline release asset
  pull-requests: write   # crap:regression / crap:improved labels

# Serializes baseline updates of consecutive merges (never cancels a running update).
concurrency:
  group: quality-${{ (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_run' || github.ref == 'refs/heads/main') && 'baseline-update' || github.run_id }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

env:
  # Threshold for functions NOT in crap-baseline.json (new or renamed code).
  CRAP_THRESHOLD: '8'
  CRAP4JS_REPO: 'IstiN/crap4js'
  CRAP4JS_REF: '83ee6201e554a91d51c298f045c5c4cb47317b6d'
  BASELINE_TAG: 'crap-baseline'
  BASELINE_ASSET: 'crap-baseline.json'

jobs:
  gate:
    # PR / dispatch on a PR head: always measure. Main-side events (push, merge-bot completion,
    # manual dispatch on main): measure only when the released baseline does not yet cover HEAD.
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    outputs:
      run: ${{ steps.g.outputs.run }}
    steps:
      - id: g
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          REF: ${{ github.ref }}
          BOT_CONCLUSION: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.conclusion }}
        run: |
          main_side=false
          [ "$EVENT" = "push" ] || [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && main_side=true
          [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_dispatch" ] && [ "$REF" = "refs/heads/main" ] && main_side=true
          if [ "$main_side" != "true" ]; then
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; exit 0      # pull_request / dispatch on a PR head: always measure
          fi
          if [ "$EVENT" = "workflow_run" ] && [ "$BOT_CONCLUSION" != "success" ]; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "merge bot run was not successful — skip"; exit 0
          fi
          body="$(gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --json body --jq .body 2>/dev/null || true)"
          if printf '%s' "$body" | grep -q "main@${GITHUB_SHA}"; then
            echo "run=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; echo "baseline already covers ${GITHUB_SHA} — skip"
          else
            echo "run=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  crap:
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.run == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20

node-version: 20

      - name: Install pinned tools (separate prefix — never node_modules here)
        run: |
          npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools" --no-fund --no-audit \
            "github:${CRAP4JS_REPO}#${CRAP4JS_REF}" nyc@17

      - name: Instrument the tree (harness eval-loads bypass nyc's hook)
        run: |
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/nyc" instrument --cwd . . \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          # nyc instrument copies only .js — add the json/md/sh payloads the
          # suite reads (configs, instructions, prompts, fixtures).
          rsync -a --exclude '*.js' --exclude '.git' ./ "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/"
          # (the factory board — and its pristine-app source guard — moved to
          # the dmtools-factory repo; nothing browser-side is text-read here anymore)
          # Tests call `git ls-files` (agentDocsCoverage): give the copied tree a throwaway
          # index of the same tracked files, without the real history.
          (cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst" && git init -q && git add -A -f . >/dev/null 2>&1 || true)

      - name: Run the unit suite for coverage (instrumented tree)
        # Canonical green-gate is the dmtools-java runner (pack-release test job); the node
        # harness mirrors it (file_*/cli_*/assert/network-guard parity) and must be green too,
        # so a red harness fails this job instead of being swallowed. ci/run_with_coverage.js
        # wraps the harness and dumps the Istanbul global after the run.
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst"
          FILES="$(node -e "console.log(require('./js/unit-tests/run_all.json').params.jobParams.testFiles.join(' '))")"
          node ci/run_with_coverage.js \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/inst/js/unit-tests/node_testRunner.js" \
            "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" $FILES

      - name: Fetch the released baseline
        id: baseline
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          if gh release download "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --pattern "$BASELINE_ASSET" \
               --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/base" --clobber 2>/dev/null && [ -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" ]; then
            echo "present=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "baseline: $(node -e "const b=require('$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")"
          else
            echo "present=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::no $BASELINE_TAG release asset yet — bootstrapping from this run"
          fi

      - name: crap4js ratchet (compare with the released baseline)
        id: ratchet
        if: steps.baseline.outputs.present == 'true'
        run: |
          set +e
          # Redirect to a file (never a pipe): the report is ~500 KB and the verdict block comes last.
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js" . \
            --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" \
            --threshold "${CRAP_THRESHOLD}" \
            --baseline "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          code=$?
          head -30 "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"
          sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          if grep -q '^improved ' "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap.txt"; then echo "improved=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"; fi
          exit $code

      - name: Update the released baseline (main only — ratchets down, never up)
        if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && github.event_name != 'pull_request' && (steps.ratchet.outcome == 'success' || steps.baseline.outputs.present != 'true')
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -e
          CRAP="$RUNNER_TEMP/tools/node_modules/.bin/crap4js"
          NOTES="Rolling per-function CRAP baseline used by the Quality workflow. Updated after every merge to main; not a product release. Measured at main@${GITHUB_SHA}"
          OUT="$RUNNER_TEMP/baseline-out/$BASELINE_ASSET"
          mkdir -p "$(dirname "$OUT")"
          # Full report (every function) for the README badges; ratchet steps keep their own outputs.
          "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold 99999 > "$RUNNER_TEMP/crap-all.txt" || true
          if [ "${{ steps.baseline.outputs.present }}" = "true" ]; then
            cp "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET" "$OUT"
            "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold "$CRAP_THRESHOLD" \
              --baseline "$OUT" --update-baseline > "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt"
            sed -n '/^CRAP Ratchet/,$p' "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
            if cmp -s "$OUT" "$RUNNER_TEMP/base/$BASELINE_ASSET"; then
              echo "baseline unchanged — nothing to upload (marker refreshed)"
              gh release edit "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --notes "$NOTES"
              exit 0
            fi
          else
            "$CRAP" . --coverage "$RUNNER_TEMP/cov/coverage-final.json" --threshold "$CRAP_THRESHOLD" \
              --baseline "$OUT" --write-baseline > "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt"
          fi
          tail -1 "$RUNNER_TEMP/update.txt"
          if gh release view "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            gh release upload "$BASELINE_TAG" "$OUT" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --clobber
          else
            gh release create "$BASELINE_TAG" "$OUT" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --prerelease --latest=false \
              --title "CRAP baseline (rolling)" \
              --notes "Rolling per-function CRAP baseline used by the Quality workflow. Updated after every merge to main; not a product release."
          fi
          # Marker the 'gate' job reads to skip runs when the baseline already covers main's HEAD.
          gh release edit "$BASELINE_TAG" --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --notes "$NOTES"
          echo "baseline released: $(node -e "const b=require('$OUT');console.log(Object.keys(b.functions).length+' functions, max '+b.maxCrap)")" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

      - name: Publish README badges (main only — data lives on the 'badges' branch)

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for GitHub PR re…

## Problem
`js/writeContentOutput.js::action` **61.9** and `js/writeSolutionAndLabels.js::buildMarkdownSection` **42** write generated content and labels back to trackers. Output text and tracker payloads must stay byte-identical.

## Goal
Bring each named function under CRAP 30 by extracting pure parse/build/decide helpers and covering every branch with characterization tests. Same tracker/SCM/git/file calls in the same order.

## Acceptance
- Behaviour unchanged; each named function at or below the target; no regression; CI `crap` check green and the node harness stays green (canonical runner: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`).
- No code path removed; uncovered paths get a characterization test.

## Rules (read before starting)
- **Pure refactor, behaviour-preserving, backward compatible.** Same exports, same signatures, same return shapes, same log lines/side effects, same tracker/SCM calls in the same order. No config or API changes.
- **Tests first:** add characterization tests that pin the current behaviour of the paths you touch (the node harness: `dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json`), then extract pure helpers (`parse*`/`build*`/`decide*`) from the big function and test those directly. Raising coverage on the function counts as much as splitting it.
- **CRAP gate:** Quality/`crap` compares this PR with the released baseline (`crap-baseline` release). The target function must go DOWN, no function may go up, new functions must be <= 8 (CRAP = CC² + CC at 0% coverage, so an untested helper needs CC <= 2 — or cover it). `crap:improved` is set automatically when it dropped. The baseline is updated by CI after the merge — do **not** commit a baseline file.
- Measure locally: `node ci/run_with_coverage.js …` then `crap4js . --coverage … --threshold 8 --baseline <released crap-baseline.json>` (see .github/workflows/quality.yml).
